excerpt: Our safety stack addresses a broad spectrum of risks, including many with harms below this severity.
paraphrase: OpenAI notes its broader safety stack covers risks below the severe harm threshold too.

excerpt: In choosing to set a high bar here, we aim to ensure that the most severe risks receive attention commensurate with their magnitude.
paraphrase: OpenAI explains it set a high severity bar so the most severe risks get proportionate attention.

excerpt: We believe there are a limited number of AI capabilities that could pose new risks of severe harm.
paraphrase: OpenAI believes only a limited set of AI capabilities pose new severe harm risks.

excerpt: In order to safely unlock the beneficial uses of frontier AI capabilities, we exercise particular caution and implement safeguards that sufficiently minimize the risk of severe harm in these areas.
paraphrase: OpenAI exercises caution and implements safeguards to minimize severe harm risk while unlocking beneficial uses.
Lead-in to the list of activities OpenAI undertakes.

excerpt: Decide where to focus – we use a holistic risk assessment to decide which frontier capability categories to track or research further, and to define threshold levels of those capabilities that are associated with meaningful increases in risk of severe harm.
paraphrase: OpenAI uses holistic risk assessment to select which capability categories to track and to set thresholds tied to meaningful risk increases.

excerpt: Measure capabilities associated with risks of severe harms – we run in–scope models through frontier capability evaluations to measure the full extent of model capabilities before we deploy our models and during development.
paraphrase: OpenAI runs in-scope models through capability evaluations both before deployment and during development.

context_stem: Measure capabilities associated with risks of severe harms —
excerpt: Our capability elicitation efforts are designed to detect the threshold levels of capability that we have identified as enabling meaningful increases in risk of severe harms.
paraphrase: Capability elicitation efforts aim to detect when identified risk-relevant capability thresholds are reached.

excerpt: Safeguard against severe harms – we evaluate the likelihood that severe harms could actually occur in the context of deployment, using threat models that take our safeguards into account.
paraphrase: OpenAI evaluates likelihood of severe harm occurring in deployment context using threat models incorporating safeguards.

excerpt: We do not deploy models that reach a High capability threshold until the associated risks that they pose are sufficiently minimized.
paraphrase: Models reaching High capability thresholds are not deployed until their risks are sufficiently minimized.

excerpt: If a model under development reaches a Critical capability threshold, we also require safeguards to sufficiently minimize the associated risks during development, irrespective of deployment plans.
paraphrase: Models reaching Critical capability thresholds during development require safeguards regardless of deployment plans.

excerpt: Build trust – we engage with subject–matter experts across and beyond OpenAI to inform these efforts and to build confidence that we are meeting our commitments and effectively managing risk.
paraphrase: OpenAI engages internal and external experts to build confidence it is meeting commitments and managing risk effectively.

excerpt: An internal, cross-functional group of OpenAI leaders called the Safety Advisory Group (SAG) oversees the Preparedness Framework and makes expert recommendations on the level and type of safeguards required for deploying frontier capabilities safely and securely.
paraphrase: The Safety Advisory Group, a cross-functional internal leadership group, oversees the Framework and recommends safeguard levels and types.

excerpt: OpenAI Leadership can approve or reject these recommendations, and our Board’s Safety and Security Committee provides oversight of these decisions.
paraphrase: OpenAI Leadership approves or rejects SAG recommendations, with Board oversight via the Safety and Security Committee.
